back: delay = min(cap, base × 2^attempt). Each failure doubles the wait, up to a cap.
sleep = random(0, min(cap, base × 2^attempt)). Spreads retries from clients that failed together.

front: Why does backoff without jitter still cause spikes?
back: Clients that failed at the same moment follow the same schedule, so they retry in synchronised waves.

front: Retry amplification across 3 layers of 3 attempts?
back: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 calls to the bottom layer for one request. Retry at one layer or use a retry budget.

front: Which errors should not be retried?
back: Permanent ones: validation failures, 400s, missing entities. They fail the same way every time.
A message that fails every time it is processed, however often it is retried.

front: Poison message in an ordered stream?
back: Head-of-line blocking: the partition or message group can't advance past it, so everything behind waits.
How long a received message stays hidden from other consumers (30 s default). Not deleted in time, it reappears.
A separate queue where messages go after too many failed attempts, so the main queue keeps flowing.
Names the DLQ and a maxReceiveCount; messages received more times than that are moved to the DLQ.
Reject without requeue, message TTL expiry, queue length overflow, quorum-queue delivery limit exceeded.
Moving messages from a DLQ back to the source queue after the fix. Do it at a throttled rate.

front: Does Kafka have a broker-side DLQ?
back: No. Clients or frameworks (Kafka Connect, Spring Kafka) publish failed records to a dead-letter topic.
A slow downstream making the upstream slow down (block, reject, drop) instead of letting work pile up.

front: Best lag metric for a queue?
back: Age of the oldest message (or consumer lag in seconds): how far behind you really are.
basic.qos limit on unacknowledged messages a consumer may hold; the broker stops delivering at the limit.
One consumer hoards messages while others idle, high latency, big redelivery bursts after a crash.
